blocks.text: The Holy Wisdom Which Attests the Dharma

inline.s: At that time the World-Honored One, having spoken the Dharma in the palace of the Dragon King, after seven days came forth from the great sea. Immeasurable hundreds of millions of Brahma gods, Shakra, world-protectors, and hosts of dragons and devas came to welcome the Buddha. Then the Tathagata raised his eyes and beheld the great city of Lanka upon Mount Malaya, and straightway smiled, saying: All the Tathagatas of the past, Arhats and fully and perfectly Enlightened Ones, all preached in this very city the Dharma of the Holy Wisdom they themselves had realized — not the realm of the speculative, perverse views of the heterodox, nor the cultivation of the two vehicles. Now I too shall reveal this Dharma to King Ravana.

At that time the World-Honored One, having taught the Dharma in the palace of the Dragon King, came forth from the great sea after seven days. The great Brahma king, Shakra, and the four world-protecting kings, leading immeasurable billions of devas and dragons, came to welcome the Buddha. Then the World-Honored One looked about and beheld the great city of Lanka upon Mount Malaya, and straightway smiled, saying: In times past all the Buddhas, without exception, proclaimed in this very city the Dharma they themselves had realized as Holy Wisdom — which is not the realm of the speculative, perverse views of the heterodox, nor the cultivation of the two vehicles. Now I too shall reveal to King Ravana this Dharma of the Holy Wisdom realized by oneself (the method whereby Shakyamuni Buddha himself perfectly realized Buddhahood).

[Shakra, world-protectors, and the hosts of dragons and devas] Brahma: the great Brahma king. Shakra: Indra, lord of the Trayastrimsha heaven. World-protectors: the four heavenly kings. The hosts of dragons and devas: the eight classes of devas and dragons. [The Holy Wisdom realized by oneself] The method of cultivation whereby the Buddha himself realized Holy Wisdom (Buddhahood). [Holy Wisdom] The wisdom that rightly illumines the ultimate truth and is free from false discrimination is called Holy Wisdom. The Tang translation says:

“Mahamati, the great bodhisattva, relying on the holy teachings, engages in no discrimination. Dwelling alone in quiet seclusion, he contemplates self-awakening, not awakened by another, free from the view of discrimination, ascending ever higher until he enters the Tathagata stage. Such cultivation is called the course of the self-realized Holy Wisdom.”

[Tathagata, Arhat, fully Enlightened] Tathagata, Arhat, and fully and perfectly Enlightened One are three of the Buddha's ten epithets. Tathagata: riding the path of Suchness, he passes from cause to fruit and realizes perfect enlightenment. Arhat: worthy of the offerings of humans and devas. Fully and perfectly Enlightened One: the true, universal, and equal enlightenment — that is, the Buddha's enlightenment. [The two vehicles] The sravaka vehicle and the pratyekabuddha vehicle. Those who awaken through cultivating the Dharma of the four noble truths are collectively the sravaka vehicle; those who awaken through cultivating the twelve links of dependent arising are collectively the pratyekabuddha vehicle.
“Now I too shall reveal this Dharma to King Ravana.”
: Now I too shall reveal to King Ravana this Dharma of the Holy Wisdom realized by oneself (revealing the Dharma the Buddha himself realized as Holy Wisdom). This is the center of this sutra.

blocks.text: Requesting the Buddha to Speak the Dharma

inline.s: At that time Ravana, king of the yakshas, through the Buddha's spiritual power heard the Buddha's voice and knew from afar that the Tathagata had come forth from the dragon palace, surrounded by Brahma, Shakra, world-protectors, devas, and dragons. Seeing the waves of the sea, he contemplated the great ocean of the alaya-consciousness of his own assembly; as the wind of the objective world stirred, the waves of the evolving consciousness arose. Filled with joy, he proclaimed aloud in his city: I shall go to the Buddha and beg him to enter this city, that I and all the devas and humans may in the long night obtain great benefit.

At this time Ravana, king of the yakshas, through the Buddha's spiritual power heard the Buddha's voice and knew from afar that the World-Honored One had come forth from the dragon palace, surrounded by the great Brahma king, Shakra, the four world-protecting kings, and hosts of devas and dragons. Seeing the great sea surging with waves, he reflected that the ocean of the alaya-consciousness of the gathered assembly likewise rose in waves under the blowing of the wind of the objective world, becoming the ocean of the evolving consciousness. Thereupon he rejoiced, and proclaimed aloud within his city of Lanka: I shall go to see the World-Honored One and beg him to enter this city and preach the wondrous principle that causes the waves of the evolving consciousness of all beings to subside and the ocean of mind to become clear — that I and all the devas and humans may in the long night of ignorance obtain great benefit.
[Alaya-consciousness] The fundamental nature (the Tathagata-garbha).
[Evolving consciousness] The nature of consciousness. (Regarding self-nature, fundamental nature, and the nature of consciousness, see
Mind, Self-Nature, and the Tathagata-Garbha

Having spoken these words, accompanied by his retinue, he rode in a palace of flowers to the place of the World-Honored One. Having arrived, he descended from the palace, circled to the right three times, and offered music and song in worship of the Tathagata. The instruments he held were all of great blue indra-gems, inlaid with lapis lazuli and other jewels, and wrapped in priceless fine garments. Their sound was exquisite, the notes harmonious; and he spoke a gatha praising the Buddha:
Having spoken these words, King Ravana and his retinue rode
in a palace of flowers (a palace adorned with wondrous flowers) and went forward

to the place of the World-Honored One. Upon arriving, he descended from the palace and circled to the right three times, offering music and dance in worship of the World-Honored One. The instruments he held were all of great blue indra-gems, inlaid with lapis lazuli and other jewels, and wrapped in priceless fine garments. Their sound was exquisite, the notes harmonious and elegant. And in this he spoke a gatha praising the Buddha:
[Ji (
ji
) le]
Music and dance.
The treasury of Mind's self-nature, without self, freed from the defilement of views; the knowledge of realized wisdom — O Buddha, please proclaim it for us.
The wondrous principle of mind and self-nature — without self and free from discrimination and clinging — is what the self-realized Holy Wisdom knows; may the Buddha proclaim it for us.

[Treasury of Dharma] The teaching of the Buddha; because the teaching contains and stores many meanings, it is called the treasury of Dharma. [No-self] No self of persons and no self of dharmas (see the note on “the two selves” later). [Defilement of views] As for “view” (an opinion or standpoint), it is clinging and discrimination. When clinging and discrimination arise, that is called the defilement of views.

Good dharmas are his body; the realized wisdom is his ever-bliss. Sovereign of free transformation, may he enter the city of Lanka. The Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the past have all dwelt within this city. This host of yakshas, of one mind, longs only to hear the Dharma.

Gathering good dharmas as his own practice, he attains Holy Wisdom and abides forever in bliss; O great World-Honored One, sovereign of free transformation, may you enter the city of Lanka and preach for us this most wondrous Dharma. The Buddhas and great bodhisattvas of the past have all dwelt within this city. This host of yakshas, of one mind, longs only to hear the Dharma.
[Good dharmas]

Dharmas that are reasonable and beneficial; thus the five precepts and the ten good actions are the good dharmas of the world, while the three studies and the six perfections are the good dharmas of the world-transcending.
At that time Ravana, king of Lanka, having praised the Buddha with the tone of the Dutaka melody, again spoke a verse in song:
At that time Ravana, king of Lanka, having praised the Buddha with the Dutaka melody, again spoke a verse in song:
[Dutaka melody]
A certain rhythmic cadence used in singing and in praise.

The World-Honored One abode seven days in the sea, then came from the dragon palace and calmly rose to this shore. I, with my maidens, the yaksha train, and Sukasrana the wise among the host, all came by their spiritual power to the Tathagata's place. Each descended his flower-palace, bowing to the world's honored one; and again by the Buddha's awesome might, each before the Buddha declared his own name:

The World-Honored One dwelt for seven days in the ocean of Magadha; then he came forth from the dragon palace and calmly rose to this shore. I, with my maidens, the yaksha retinue, and Sukasrana, the wisest in the assembly, all by their spiritual power came before the World-Honored One. Each descended from his flower-palace and bowed in homage to the world's honored one (the World-Honored One); and again, through the Buddha's awesome might, each declared his own name before the Buddha:
[Maidens]
Palace women.

I am the rakshasa king, ten-headed Ravana; now have I come to the Buddha's place. O Buddha, receive me and all beings dwelling in the city of Lanka. The countless Buddhas of the past all ascended the jewel-mountain's summit, abode in Lanka's city, and preached the Dharma self-realized. So should the World-Honored One abide upon that jewel-adorned hill, mid a bodhisattva throng, and speak the pure Dharma. We today, with the dwellers of Lanka, of one mind together, long to hear the wordless self-realized Dharma.

I am the rakshasa king, ten-headed Ravana; today I have come before the Buddha. O Buddha, receive me and all beings in the city of Lanka. The countless Buddhas of the past all ascended to the summit of Lanka, dwelt in the city of Lanka, and preached the Dharma of self-realized Holy Wisdom. The World-Honored One should likewise abide in the city of Lanka adorned with countless jewels, surrounded by the host of bodhisattvas, preaching this pure Dharma. We today, with the great assembly in the city of Lanka, of one mind together, long to hear the wordless Dharma of self-realized Holy Wisdom.
[The jewel-mountain's peak] The summit of Mount Lanka. The Entry of Lanka Sutra, in the chapter on the Buddha's Invitation, says:

“That mountain was formed of manifold precious substances, the gems inlaid one with another, radiant and blazing, like a mountain of gold illumined by a hundred thousand suns. Moreover, there were countless gardens of flowers and fragrant trees, all groves of jewel-perfumed forests; the gentle breeze struck them, swaying the branches and stirring the leaves, and a hundred thousand subtle fragrances were at once diffused while a hundred thousand subtle sounds arose together. The layered crags wound in and out, and everywhere were the halls of sages, the chambers of spirits, and stone chapels, formed of countless gems, transparent within and without, so that the light of sun and moon could no longer appear — all these were places where the immortals and sages of old, contemplating the Dharma of reality as it is, attained the Way.”
[Self-realized Dharma] The Dharma of self-realized Holy Wisdom.

I mind the Buddhas of all times, the countless Ones, round whom bodhisattvas throng, preaching the Lanka's words. This Entry-Lanka scripture, praised by the Buddhas gone — O Buddha, as the supreme of old, unfold it to the assembly. I beg you, for the countless yaksha host your pity's due, to enter that jewel-adorned city and this wondrous Door renew.

I call to mind all the countless Buddhas of the ages past, preaching the Lanka Sutra surrounded by hosts of bodhisattvas. This Entry of Lanka scripture was praised by the Buddhas of old; O Buddha, like the Buddhas of the past, do you also unfold it for the assembly. I beg the Buddha, out of compassion for the countless yaksha host, to enter the city of Lanka adorned with many jewels, and speak this Door of the wondrous Dharma.

Wondrous is this city of Lanka, adorned with jewels of many kinds; its walls are not of earth and stone, its nets all treasures fine. This yaksha host once made offerings to the Buddha, their cultivation free from all faults, their realization ever clear. Yaksha men and women thirst for the Great Vehicle, themselves believing in Mahayana, and glad that others abide in it.

Wondrous is this city of Lanka, adorned with jewels of many kinds; its walls are not of earth and stone, and its nets are all formed of precious gems. This yaksha host once made offerings to the Buddha, and their cultivation was free from all faults, and their realization ever clear. Yaksha men and women, thirsting for the Great Vehicle, themselves believed in the Great Vehicle and were glad to let others believe in it.
[Mahayana] An abbreviation of Mahayana, rendered in Chinese as the Great Vehicle.

We pray the supreme of the world, for the rakshasa host and the jar-eared retinue, to come to the city of Lanka. In the past, the future, and the present I have diligently made offerings to the Buddhas; I long to hear the self-realized Dharma, the ultimate and Great Vehicle's path. May the Buddha, pitying me and this yaksha host, with all the sons of the Buddha, enter this city of Lanka. My palace, my maidens, and all my garlands, and my delightful garden of no-sorrow — may the Buddha in compassion receive them. Toward the Buddhas and bodhisattvas I withhold nothing, even my own body in service — we pray you receive them in compassion.

We pray the supreme of the world (the World-Honored One), for the rakshasa host and the jar-eared retinue and others, to come to the city of Lanka. In the past, the future, and the present I have diligently made offerings to the Buddhas; I long to hear the Dharma of self-realized Holy Wisdom, the ultimate path of the Great Vehicle. May the Buddha pity me and this yaksha host, together with the great bodhisattvas, and enter this city of Lanka. My palace, my maidens, and all my garlands, and my lovely garden of no-sorrow — I offer all to the Buddha; may the Buddha pity us and receive them. Toward the Buddhas and bodhisattvas I withhold nothing, even my own body in tender service — we pray the World-Honored One, out of compassion, to receive it.
[Jar (
weng
) eared] A description of the rakshas' ears being as large as jars.

At that time the World-Honored One, having heard these words, told him: O yaksha king, the great teachers (the Buddhas) of past ages, all pitying you, accepted your invitation, went to the jewel-mountain and preached the self-realized Dharma; the Buddhas of the future shall do likewise. This is the dwelling place of those who cultivate the deep contemplation and abide in the bliss of the Dharma in this very life; I and the bodhisattvas, pitying you, accept your invitation. Having spoken these words, he remained silent.

At that time the World-Honored One, having heard these words of King Ravana, told him: O yaksha king, all the great teachers (the Buddhas) of past ages, pitying you, accepted your invitation, went to the jewel-mountain of Lanka and preached the Dharma of self-realized Holy Wisdom; so too shall the Buddhas of the future. This is the dwelling of those who cultivate deep contemplation and abide in the bliss of the Dharma in this very life; I and the bodhisattvas, out of pity for you, accept your invitation. Having spoken, the World-Honored One remained silent.
[Abiding in the bliss of the Dharma in this very life]
Cultivating meditative concentration, free from all false thinking, body and mind quiescent, one receives in this very life the bliss of Dharma-joy and abides in it steadfast.

At that time King Ravana offered the Buddha the wondrous flower-palace upon which he had ridden. The Buddha sat upon it, and the king and the bodhisattvas went before and behind to lead and follow; countless maidens sang and praised, making offerings to the Buddha, and they went to that city. Upon arriving at that city, King Ravana and his retinue made manifold superior offerings. The boys and girls among the yaksha host offered the Buddha a net of jewels. King Ravana made an offering of a precious garland and hung it upon the neck of the Buddha and the bodhisattvas. Then the World-Honored One and the bodhisattvas, having received the offerings, each in brief set forth the profoundly deep Dharma of the self-realized realm.

At that time King Ravana offered the Buddha the wondrous flower-palace on which he had ridden. The Buddha sat upon it, and King Ravana and the bodhisattvas went before and behind to lead and follow; countless maidens sang and praised, making offerings to the Buddha, and they went to the city of Lanka. Upon arriving, King Ravana and his retinue made manifold superior offerings. The boys and girls among the yaksha host offered a net of jewels to the Buddha. King Ravana offered a precious garland and hung it on the neck of the Buddha and the bodhisattvas. Then the World-Honored One and the bodhisattvas, having received the offerings, each in brief set forth for King Ravana and his retinue the profoundly deep Dharma of the self-realized realm.
At that time King Ravana and his retinue made further offerings to the bodhisattva Mahamati, and exhorted him, saying:
At that time King Ravana and his retinue again made offerings to the bodhisattva Mahamati, and exhorted him, saying:

Now I invite the great one to ask the World-Honored One of the self-realized wisdom-realm of all the Tathagatas. I, with the yaksha host and these bodhisattvas, of one mind long to hear — therefore we all urge you. You are a cultivator, the most excellent in speech; therefore we revere you and urge you to ask the Dharma. The pure self-realized Dharma ultimately enters the Buddha-stage, free from the heterodox and the two vehicles, and from all their faults.

Now I respectfully invite the great being to question the World-Honored One concerning the realm of self-realized Holy Wisdom of all the Tathagatas. I, with the yaksha host and these bodhisattvas, with one mind long to hear — therefore we all urge you. You are the most excellent in speech among cultivators; therefore we revere you and urge you to ask the Dharma. The pure Dharma of self-realized Holy Wisdom ultimately enters the Buddha-stage, free from the heterodox, the two vehicles, and all their faults.

At that time the World-Honored One, by his spiritual power, transformed within that mountain countless jewel-mountains, all adorned with the wonderful gems of the devas, in the hundreds of thousands of millions. On each mountain appeared a Buddha-body; before each Buddha was King Ravana and his assembly; and all the lands in the ten directions appeared within them. In each land there was a Tathagata; before each Buddha was King Ravana with his retinue; and in the Asoka garden of the great city of Lanka, such adornment was in every way without difference. In each there arose the bodhisattva Mahamati to ask, and the Buddha revealed the realm of self-realized wisdom. Having spoken this sutra with a hundred thousand subtle sounds, the Buddha and the bodhisattvas all vanished into the sky and were seen no more.

At that time the World-Honored One, by his spiritual power, transformed within the mountain of Lanka countless Lanka-mountains, all adorned with the wonderful gems of the devas, by the hundreds of thousands of millions. On each mountain appeared a Buddha-body; before each Buddha was King Ravana with his assembly; and all the lands in the ten directions appeared within them. In each land there was a Tathagata; before each Buddha was King Ravana with his retinue; and in the Asoka garden of the great city of Lanka, such adornment was in every way the same. In each arose the bodhisattva Mahamati to ask, and the Buddha revealed to the great assembly the realm of self-realized Holy Wisdom. Having spoken this sutra with a hundred thousand subtle sounds, the Buddha and the bodhisattvas all vanished into the sky and were seen no more.

King Ravana saw only himself abiding in his own palace, and reflected: Who was it that spoke? Who heard the words? What was seen? Who was the seer? The Buddha, the cities, the multitude of jewels, mountains and forests — where are these things now? Were they made in a dream? Conceived by magic? Like the Gandharva city? Seen through a film over the eyes? Deceived by a mirage? Like the stone woman's child in a dream? Like the turning wheel of fire of smoke and flame? And he reflected again:
All dharmas are of such a nature — they are but the realm of one's own mind's discrimination.

Deluded common beings cannot understand this. There is no seer, and nothing seen; there is no speaker, and nothing spoken; seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma are all discrimination. As when one sees as before one cannot see the Buddha; when no discrimination arises then one does see him.

At that time King Ravana saw only himself abiding in his own palace, and reflected: Who was it just now speaking the Dharma? Who was hearing? What was seen? Who was the seer? The Buddha, the cities, the multitude of jewels, mountains and forests — where are these things now? Were they made in a dream? Conceived by magic? Like the Gandharva city? The flowers in the sky seen by a diseased eye? A thirsty deer deceived by a mirage? Like the stone woman dreaming she bore a child? Like the turning wheel of fire of smoke and flame? And he reflected again: All dharmas are of such a nature; they are but the realm manifested by one's own mind's discrimination. Deluded and inverted common beings cannot understand this truth. In reality there is no seer, and nothing seen; no speaker, and nothing spoken; seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma are all the realm manifested by one's own mind's discrimination. If one sees as one did just now, one cannot see the Buddha; when no discrimination arises, then one does see the Buddha.
[The Gandharva city]

Musicians are called gandharvas; they can conjure up palaces and towers for people to behold, so these conjured towers are called the Gandharva city. Mirage-like phantasms such as the sea mirage are also called the Gandharva city.

[The mirage] The vapor produced beneath the blazing sun; from afar it seems to be water, and a thirsty deer longs to drink and so runs after it, but in the end it cannot be had — it is used as a simile for illusion. [The turning fire-wheel] In darkness, when a torch is whirled, it is mistaken for a single wheel of fire — a simile for a false appearance. [Flowers in the sky] A diseased eye wrongly sees flowers in empty space — a simile for an optical illusion. [The nature of all dharmas is thus] The self-nature of all dharmas is like this. Here “self-nature” refers to the inherent, immutable, unchanging nature (essence) of each dharma. [As one sees as before one cannot see the Buddha; when no discrimination arises then one does see him] The Diamond Sutra says:
“All that has form is false and vain; if one sees all forms as non-form, then one sees the Tathagata.”

At that time the king of Lanka at once awakened, freed from all defilement, realized that it is only one's own mind, and abode in non-discrimination. Through the power of the roots of goodness planted in former times, he obtained vision of all dharmas in accordance with reality, not awakened by reliance on another. He could observe skillfully with his own wisdom, forever free from all speculative wrong interpretations, abiding in the great cultivation, a teacher of cultivators, manifesting various bodies. He was adept in skillful means, and knew the signs of advancement upon each stage; he always delighted to be free from mind, will, and consciousness, cut off the view of threefold continuity, free from the attachments of the heterodox, self-awakened within, entered the Tathagata-garbha, and advanced toward the Buddha-stage.

At that time the king of Lanka at once awakened, free from all defilement, realized that the realm is merely what one's own mind manifests, and abode in the wisdom of non-discrimination. Through the power of the roots of goodness planted in former times, he obtained vision of all dharmas in accordance with reality (seeing that all dharmas are illusory appearances), not awakened by reliance on another. He could observe skillfully with his own wisdom, forever free from all speculative wrong interpretations, abiding in the great cultivation, a teacher of cultivators, manifesting various bodies. He was adept in skillful means, and knew the signs of advancement upon each stage; he always delighted to be free from mind, will, and consciousness, cut off the view of threefold continuity, free from the attachments of the heterodox, self-awakened within, entered the Tathagata-garbha, and advanced toward the Buddha-stage.

[Vision in accordance with reality] To know that all dharmas are illusory appearances — “in the midst of seeming arising and ceasing, one sees only non-arising” — this is vision in accordance with reality; whereas sentient beings “in the midst of serene non-arising, wrongly see arising and ceasing.” (See
The Reality of All Dharmas

.) [The stages] That is, the ten stages. In the fifty-two stages of a bodhisattva's cultivation, the tenth group of ten is called the ten stages; upon these ten stages one gradually opens the Buddha-realm and accomplishes the all-knowing wisdom, already within the sage's position, whence they are also called the “ten sages.” [Mind, will, consciousness] Gathering up is called mind; reflecting is called will; distinguishing is called consciousness. Of “mind, will, and consciousness,” mind refers to the eighth consciousness (the alaya-consciousness), will refers to the seventh consciousness (the manas-consciousness), and the consciousness refers to the sixth consciousness. [Free from mind, will, and consciousness] Free from the operation of the consciousness-mind. (Regarding the operation of the consciousness-mind, see
Mind, Self-Nature, and the Tathagata-Garbha

, the section on “The Operation of the Consciousness-Mind.”) [Threefold continuity] The continuity of the world, the continuity of beings, and the continuity of karma. The continuity of the world means that because beings, deluded, continually create karma, their world of retribution is continually established; the continuity of beings means that because beings have not cut off birth and death, their five aggregates are continually and provisionally conjoined, so beings are continually constituted; the continuity of karma means that because beings continually create karma, the bitter retribution of their evil karma is continually established. [The five aggregates] The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of conditioning, and the aggregate of consciousness; these five gather and arise together, so they are called the “five aggregates”; and because they can cover over one's true nature, causing one to be deluded and inverted and to create all karmas, they are also called the “five coverings.” Of these, the aggregate of form refers to matter and is called the “dharma of form”; the four aggregates of feeling, perception, conditioning, and consciousness pertain to spirit and are called the “dharmas of mind.” These are the five great constituents of body and mind. Of them the aggregate of form is the physical body, while the other four aggregates (feeling, perception, conditioning, consciousness) are the mind. [The Tathagata-garbha] The fundamental nature. (See
Mind, Self-Nature, and the Tathagata-Garbha

He heard a voice in the sky and within the palace, saying: Excellent, O king! As you have learned, all cultivators should so learn, should so see, and all Tathagatas should be so seen. If one sees all dharmas otherwise, that is a view of annihilation. You should forever be free from mind, will, and consciousness; you should diligently contemplate all dharmas; you should cultivate inner practice, not adhere to outward views, nor fall into the two vehicles nor into the phrases and meanings the heterodox cultivate, their seen realms, nor the samadhi-dharmas that should be attained.

He heard a voice issuing from the sky and within the palace, saying: Excellent, O king! As you have learned, all cultivators should so learn, should so see, and all Tathagatas should be so seen. If one sees otherwise than this, that is a view of annihilation. You should forever be free from mind, will, and consciousness; you should diligently contemplate all dharmas; you should cultivate inner practice, not adhere to outward views, nor fall into the two vehicles nor into the phrases and meanings the heterodox cultivate, their seen realms, nor the samadhi-dharmas they should attain.

You should not delight in frivolous talk and jesting; you should not give rise to the views of the Vedas; you should not cling to the ease of kingship; nor should you dwell in the six concentrations and the like. If you can be thus, this is the practice of one who cultivates in accordance with reality: he can overthrow other doctrines, can break evil views, can abandon all clinging to the view of self, can with wondrous wisdom turn the consciousness upon which he relies, can cultivate the bodhisattva's path of the Great Vehicle, and can enter the Tathagata's realm of self-realization.

You should not delight in frivolous talk and jesting; you should not give rise to the views of the Vedas; you should not cling to the ease of the kingly position; nor should you dwell in the six concentrations and the like. If you can be thus, this is the practice of one who cultivates in accordance with reality — he can overthrow other evil doctrines, break evil views, abandon all clinging to the view of self, with wondrous wisdom turn the consciousness upon which he relies, cultivate the bodhisattva's path of the Great Vehicle, and enter the Tathagata's realm of self-realization.

[The views of the Vedas] The sayings of the four Veda books, which the heterodox Brahmins revere as spoken by Brahma. [The six concentrations] The four dhyanas of the form realm, plus the intermediate concentration and the not-yet-attained concentration. [The four dhyanas] Four concentrations, cultivating which one can be born into the four dhyana heavens of the form realm: the first dhyana, the second dhyana, the third dhyana, and the fourth dhyana.

You should thus diligently cultivate and study, causing the Dharma you have obtained to become ever purer. Skillfully cultivate samadhi and samapatti; do not cling to the realms of the two vehicles and the heterodox as supreme bliss. As the ordinary cultivator discriminates, the heterodox cling to the view of self, holding to the appearance of self, and grasping at the reality of the qualities; the two vehicles see dependent arising from ignorance, and vainly discriminate within the emptiness of self-nature.

You should thus diligently cultivate and study, causing the Dharma you have obtained to become ever purer. Skillfully cultivate samadhi and samapatti; do not cling to the realms of the two vehicles and the heterodox as supreme bliss. As the ordinary cultivator discriminates, the heterodox cling to the view of self, holding to the appearance of self, and wrongly cling to the qualities as real and so grasp at them. The two vehicles wrongly cling to the flow of the twelve links of dependent arising, beginning with ignorance conditioning formations, as real, and vainly discriminate within the emptiness of self-nature.
[Samadhi]

In Chinese it is rendered: fixed concentration. It means concentrating the mind in a single state. When a cultivator's six senses contact the six sense-objects, if he can refrain from giving rise to mind, from moving a thought, from discriminating, from clinging — that is called “fixed concentration,” which is entering the state of “samadhi.” [Samapatti] In Chinese: equal holding. Free from both drowsiness and agitation is “equal”; keeping the mind focused on a single object is “holding.” It means that one who seeks perfect enlightenment, with the pure enlightened mind, knows that the nature of mind and the sense-objects all arise from transformation, and so gives rise to transformative practice to eliminate all transformations. [Agitation] Swaying. The mind-thoughts waver and cannot be subdued. [Quality (guna)] It means: primary substance.

[The twelve links of dependent arising] The twelve links explain the process of the wandering of beings through birth and death. The twelve links are: ignorance (the afflictions of greed, hatred, and delusion are the root of birth and death), conditioning (creating various karmas), consciousness (the karmic consciousness entering the womb), name-and-form (the embryo having only a physical form, the six senses not yet complete), the six sense-entrances (the embryo growing into a human form with the six senses such as the eye), contact (on leaving the womb, contact with the external world), feeling (on contact with the external world, feeling of pleasure and pain arises), craving (toward objects, craving arises), grasping (pursuit and creation), becoming (the karmic cause that will draw on future retribution), birth (again receiving a future body of the five aggregates), aging and death (the future body gradually grows old and dies). Its process of wandering through birth and death is: ignorance conditions conditioning; conditioning conditions consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form; name-and-form conditions the six sense-entrances; the six sense-entrances condition contact; contact conditions feeling; feeling conditions craving; craving conditions grasping; grasping conditions becoming; becoming conditions birth; birth conditions aging and death. Contemplating the twelve links of dependent arising is the method of cultivation of the pratyekabuddha.

King of Lanka, this Dharma is supreme and is the path of the Great Vehicle; it can cause one to accomplish self-realized Holy Wisdom, and to receive a superior life among the various realms of existence. King of Lanka, this Great Vehicle practice breaks the film of ignorance, extinguishes the waves of consciousness, and does not fall among the evil practices of the heterodox. King of Lanka, the heterodox practitioner clings to self and composes various wrong doctrines, and cannot proclaim the two meanings of freedom from clinging and the seeing of the nature of consciousness. Excellent! King of Lanka, your having first seen the Buddha and pondered this meaning — such pondering is itself seeing the Buddha.

King of Lanka, this Dharma is supreme and is the path of the Great Vehicle; it can cause one to accomplish self-realized Holy Wisdom, and to receive a superior and marvelous life among the various realms of existence. King of Lanka, this Great Vehicle practice breaks the film of ignorance, extinguishes the waves of consciousness, and does not fall among the evil practices of the heterodox. King of Lanka, the heterodox practitioner clings to self and composes various wrong doctrines, and cannot proclaim the two meanings of freedom from clinging and the seeing of the nature of consciousness. Excellent! King of Lanka, your having first seen the Buddha and pondered this meaning — such pondering is itself seeing the Buddha.

[The various realms of existence] All realms of existence. Among “existence” there are the distinctions of the three existences, the four existences, the seven existences, the nine existences, and the twenty-five existences. [The nature of consciousness] That is, the element of consciousness. It is said that in a former kalpa the bodhisattva Maitreya, at the place of the Buddha Sun-Moon-Lamp, left the home life and cultivated the samadhi of mind-only consciousness; only when the Buddha Dipamkara appeared did he accomplish the supreme, wondrous, complete samadhi of consciousness-mind, understanding that all the lands of the Tathagatas, pure or impure, existent or non-existent, are all manifestations of the transformations of one's own mind, and so awakened into perfect penetration. Therefore he said: I contemplate that the ten directions are only consciousness; the consciousness-mind is perfectly bright, and I have attained the tolerance of non-arising — this is the foremost. [The element of consciousness] The nature of consciousness has no source; it arises because the six senses connect with the six sense-objects. When senses and objects mutually arise, discriminating [consciousness] wrongly arises. Sentient beings, confounded, merely follow discrimination and do not know that the nature of consciousness is clear, that it pervades the whole Dharma-realm, that following the minds of beings and according to karma it manifests — and because senses and objects are boundless, consciousness too is inexhaustible, containing and emitting the emptiness of the ten directions — how could it have a place? Therefore it is called the element of consciousness.

At that time King Ravana again thought: May I once more behold the Tathagata. The Tathagata, the World-Honored One, is free and at ease in all contemplation, beyond the dharmas of the heterodox; he can teach the realm of self-realized Holy Wisdom, surpassing all the works of the transformations in response; he abides in the Tathagata's fixed concentration and enters the bliss of samadhi. Therefore he is called the great teacher of contemplation, and also the great compassionate one: he can burn up the firewood of afflictions and discriminations completely, surrounded by the host of the sons of the Buddha, pervading into the minds of all beings, present everywhere, possessed of all knowledge, forever free from all discrimination of things and signs. Now I long to behold again the Tathagata's great spiritual power; because of seeing it, the unattained are attained, the attained do not regress, and freed from all discriminations, abiding in the bliss of samadhi, one grows and fulfills the Tathagata's stage of knowledge.

At that time King Ravana again thought: May I once more behold the World-Honored One. The World-Honored One is free and at ease in all contemplative practices, beyond the dharmas of the heterodox; he can teach the realm of self-realized Holy Wisdom, and surpasses all the matters of the one who transforms in response and that which is transformed; he abides in the Tathagata's fixed concentration and enters the bliss of samadhi. Therefore he is called the great teacher of contemplation and the great compassionate one. He can burn up the firewood of afflictions and discriminations completely; surrounded by the host of the sons of the Buddha, he pervades into the minds of all beings, is present everywhere, possessed of all knowledge, forever free from all discrimination of things and signs. Now I long to behold again the World-Honored One's great spiritual power; because of seeing it, the unattained are attained, the attained do not regress, and freed from all discriminations, abiding in the bliss of samadhi, one grows and fulfills the Tathagata's stage of knowledge.

At that time the World-Honored One, knowing that the king of Lanka was about to realize the tolerance of non-arising, out of compassion manifested his body, causing the objects of transformation to return as before. Then the ten-headed king saw what he had formerly seen: countless mountain-cities, all adorned with jewels; in each city was a Tathagata, an Arhat, fully and perfectly Enlightened, adorned with the thirty-two marks; and he saw his own body standing before each Buddha, each surrounded by Mahamati and the yakshas, preaching the Dharma practiced by the self-realized wisdom; and he also saw the lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions — such matters were all without any difference.

At that time the World-Honored One, knowing that the king of Lanka was about to realize the tolerance of non-arising, out of compassion manifested his body, causing the scene just vanished to reappear. Then the ten-headed king of Lanka again saw what he had just seen: countless mountain-cities of Lanka, all adorned with many jewels; in each city was a Buddha adorned with the thirty-two marks, and he saw his own body standing before each Buddha; each Buddha was surrounded by Mahamati and the yakshas, preaching the Dharma practiced by the self-realized wisdom; and he also saw that the lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions were all such a scene, without any difference.
